items.title: Monterrey Amid Mountains
items.short_description: Mexico’s second-largest metropolitan area borders on folded rock layers of the Sierra Madre Oriental.
items.abstract: Mexico’s second-largest metropolitan area borders on folded rock layers of the Sierra Madre Oriental. The spot where these folds nestle up against Mexico’s second-largest metropolitan area captured the attention of an astronaut aboard the International Space Station, who took this photo on August 26, 2026. The metropolitan area is home to 5.3 million people, according to the 2020 census. Along the city’s southern edge, layers of limestone, deposited in the late Mesozoic era and then folded between about 80 and 50 million years ago, form the Sierra Madre Oriental. But its channel is crucial for collecting runoff from summer rains and serves as an important natural area for plant and animal life within the city. Near the city’s border with the Sierra Madre Oriental sits Universidad de Monterrey, a host venue for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

items.title: Dust Storm Sweeps Over Mali
items.short_description: At a time of year when dust storm activity winds down, a plume of dust blanketed parts of the West African nation and its neighbors.
items.abstract: At a time of year when dust storm activity winds down, a plume of dust blanketed parts of the West African nation and its neighbors. As summer winds down in West Africa, so does much of the region’s dust activity. Dust storms can still occur, though, as one did in early September 2026, when a plume covered parts of Mali and neighboring countries. According to Tianle Yuan, an atmospheric scientist at NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center, storms like this one are often associated with haboobs —powerful dust storms driven by strong convective winds. For instance, Yuan noted that the phenomenon can affect dust over the Sahel and Mali by shifting the Intertropical Convergence Zone and altering convection patterns, though the influence cuts both ways.

items.title: Anak Krakatau Rumbles Again
items.short_description: A powerful eruption from the Indonesian volcano lofted ash into the atmosphere, disrupting thousands of flights and degrading air quality.
items.abstract: A powerful eruption from the Indonesian volcano lofted ash into the atmosphere, disrupting thousands of flights and degrading air quality. Eruptions are a regular occurrence at Anak Krakatau, a small volcano between the Indonesian islands of Java and Sumatra. The presence of ash in the atmosphere prompted the temporary closure of eight airports on Java and Sumatra, disrupting nearly 3,000 flights in and out of the area, according to news reports. Ashfall affected populated areas, particularly to the east of Anak Krakatau in Jakarta and other parts of West Java, the Indonesian Humanitarian Coordination Platform (IHCP) reported. However, this air quality hazard differs from the smoke produced by peatland fires elsewhere in the country in terms of particle characteristics, dispersal patterns, and protection measures, the IHCP noted. On September 6, the continuous explosive eruption from Anak Krakatau subsided, though the volcano kept rumbling.

items.title: The Otherworldly Geology of Vasquez Rocks
items.short_description: Layers of sedimentary rock that jut from the Soledad Basin at surprising angles have long enthralled television and film producers, including the team behind Star Trek.
items.abstract: Layers of sedimentary rock that jut from the Soledad Basin at surprising angles have long enthralled television and film producers, including the team behind Star Trek. Several of the outcrops at Vasquez Rocks Natural Area in Southern California jut from the arid landscape of the Soledad Basin at remarkable angles. That's fitting, in some ways, because the rocks have served as one of the Star Trek franchise's favorite backdrops ever since the show's inaugural season, when Captain James T. Eventually this tectonic activity led to the uplift and deformation of the Soledad Basin, with sedimentary layers gradually tilting, folding, and rotating. They make appearances in dozens of other television shows and movies, including the science fiction series Westworld, For All Mankind, and Battlestar Galactica.

items.title: A Bright Spot at Mount Michael
items.short_description: With austral winter nearing its end, clouds cleared for a satellite view of volcanic activity in the remote South Atlantic.
items.abstract: With austral winter nearing its end, clouds cleared for a satellite view of volcanic activity in the remote South Atlantic. Mount Michael, the stratovolcano at the center of Saunders Island, rises above the ice-filled South Atlantic Ocean in this image, acquired with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on the NASA-USGS Landsat 8 satellite on August 24, 2026. Because of the volcanoes’ remoteness, scientists rely on satellite data to understand their activity. Data provided through MIROVA, a near-real-time volcanic hot spot detection system, indicate that low-intensity activity has been ongoing at the volcano for the past several years. Other observations from NASA's Aura satellite show that emissions of sulfur dioxide and other gases are common at Mount Michael. False-color imagery captured by NASA’s Aqua satellite indicates that a volcanic track caused by degassing sulfur dioxide was likely present as well.

items.title: A Trio of Tropical Cyclones in the Pacific
items.short_description: The Pacific was buzzing with storms while the Atlantic was notably quiet.
items.abstract: The Pacific was buzzing with storms while the Atlantic was notably quiet. In early September, near the climatological peak of hurricane season, those spring outlooks were on target, with the eastern Pacific buzzing with activity and the Atlantic notably quiet. As of September 3, the Northeast Pacific had produced 15 named storms and six hurricanes, well above the norm for that point in the season. Pacific Daylight Time (20:14 Universal Time) on September 1, NASA’s EPIC (Earth Polychromatic Imaging Camera) on the DSCOVR (Deep Space Climate Observatory) satellite captured an image of three tropical cyclones churning simultaneously in the Pacific, along with one in the Atlantic. In the Atlantic, Tropical Storm Edouard was visible to EPIC over Louisiana and Texas, shortly after the short-lived storm made landfall.

items.title: Drought Intensifies Across Puerto Rico
items.short_description: Rainfall deficits and high temperatures have created unusually dry conditions and have spurred water shortages on much of the tropical archipelago.
items.abstract: Rainfall deficits and high temperatures have created unusually dry conditions and have spurred water shortages on much of the tropical archipelago. The dry conditions have contributed to water shortages and rationing in some areas, leading Puerto Rico’s governor to declare a state of emergency in late July and the U.S. government to issue a drought disaster declaration for more than two dozen cities and towns in late August. For recent updates to Puerto Rico’s drought maps, satellite estimates of soil moisture, as well as weather, streamflow, and well observations, were particularly important factors, he said. As of August 25, 2026, three-quarters of Puerto Rico was experiencing at least moderate drought, according to the group’s assessment. Strained water resources have affected farmers, ranchers, and residents across the territory.
